lessons.title: First Watt
lessons.concept: Power: kW is a rate, capacity is a ceiling, and load above capacity means a blackout.
lessons.goal: Two racks, one day, no blackouts.

steps.text: Build your first rack on the glowing slot
say: Bea. Power. Welcome to the hall. One job today: two racks, a full day, nothing goes dark.
Racks tab in the build bar, pick the AC-1, drop it on the glowing slot. Everything else is locked till it's in. Don't touch the rest. I mean it.
after: Hear that? 40 kW, flat out. A {{kw|kW}} is a rate: how hard something pulls right now. The bar at the top is the whole hall, 93 kW, against a feeder that gives 120. Remember the 120. I will quiz you.

steps.text: Build a second rack on the next slot
say: {{capacity|Capacity}} is the most a supply can give. This feeder tops out at 120 kW. The hall burns 53 before a single rack works (air handler, lift, the intake itself). One rack takes it to 93. Put the second one in and watch the bar.
after: And there it goes. Two racks want 133 kW, the feeder gives 120, and the breaker does what breakers do. Load over capacity is a blackout. Every time. The whole job is keeping capacity above load, with {{headroom|headroom}} to spare.
Power overlay's on so you can see the net. Next part, I hate: a generator.

steps.text: Add the diesel generator in Power
say: Power tab. Diesel Genset. Glowing slot. It starts itself when the grid can't keep up.

A {{genset|generator}} adds capacity: 120 from the feeder, plus 800 from the diesel. It also adds smoke, and smoke doesn't wash out. Today it's the right tool. Later I'll show you better ones, and you'll feel bad.
after: That gap between what you can supply and what you're using is {{headroom|headroom}}. Loads of it now. Hold both racks flat out for one game day and you pass.

steps.text: Hold both racks at full load for one day
say: Let the clock run. Keep headroom above 10% all day and don't let anything go dark. I'll watch the meter. And the exhaust.

lessons.learned: {{kw|kW}} is how hard equipment pulls right now. {{capacity|Capacity}} is the most the supply can give. Keep capacity above load, with {{headroom|headroom}} to spare.
lessons.outro: Two racks, a whole day, lights on. Okay. That's good. Next time I'll show you power that doesn't come out of a tank. Find me when you want to know where all this heat goes. Cass will be there. She'll ask if you slept.
